what: a modelled thread on a hole that isn't the thread's size: refused with the size to use, never a silent change of the hole
method: Decision (#1018, #2853): a modelled thread never changes the size of the hole it is on; one that isn't the thread's size is refused, naming the size to use. A fill-to-tap-drill or turn-down option would be opt-in, off by default (see #3060), and get its own case. The refusal's numbers, from ISO 68-1 (H = P sqrt3/2, basic depth 5H/8): M20 (P 2.5): tap drill = 20 - 2.5 = 17.5 mm; depth 5H/8 = 5/8 x 2.5 x sqrt3/2 = 1.353 mm; the 20 mm hole is at the major diameter. Expected message: "this 20 mm hole is too wide for a modelled M20 thread: it would cut 0.00 mm of the thread's 1.35 mm depth; drill 17.5 mm for M20, or thread this hole M22".
refusal: this 20 mm hole is too wide for a modelled M20 thread: it would cut 0.00 mm of the thread's 1.35 mm depth; drill 17.5 mm for M20, or thread this hole M22
